## Report: "Oral recPrP^Sc causes prion disease in wild-type mice"

### 1. The question, frozen

The title is missing, so I take the question the opening and closing of §1 make central: **did a single oral feeding of in-vitro-made recPrP^Sc give wild-type mice prion disease, and does that show PrP^Sc causes orally transmitted prion disease?** Kind: mostly *what produces it?* (feed → disease), with a piece of *what can we tell from what we see?* (low rate → digestion, dose).

Range: one batch of recPrP^Sc, 11 fed mice, 6-week-old female C57BL/6, one dried pellet each, watched to 650 days; passage done by injection, not by mouth.

Jobs, as contrasts: why mouse #9 and not the other ten recPrP^Sc-fed mice; why the substrate-fed mice got none; why #9's brain transmits but #10/#14's does not; why 1 in 11 by mouth against 100% by injection.

### 2. The parts

(A) recPrP^Sc made from recombinant PrP plus non-protein cofactors. (B) One dried pellet, one mouse per cage, eaten whole. (C) The dose fed (~5 LogLD50, inferred). (D) #9 (and #19, DBH-fed) fell ill at ~250 days. (E) PK-resistant PrP plus spongiosis, astrogliosis, microgliosis in those two mice only. (F) Their brain homogenate transmits fatally by injection (~190 days). (G) Clasping-only donors and normal donors do not transmit. (H) The sPMCA substrate control causes nothing. (I) "recPrP^Sc survives digestion." (J) Attack rate is "comparable to naturally occurring prions."

### 3. Part by part

| Part | Mark | Also |
|---|---|---|
| A recPrP^Sc | **Held** | Feed plain substrate instead: no disease. Same batch by injection: 100% at 196 days. The substrate group's size is not given. |
| B single pellet, eaten whole | **Held** | This is what makes "single feeding suffices" a claim at all. The mass of PrP per pellet is unstated. |
| C dose ~5 LogLD50 | **Borrowed** | Rests on 10^4 LD50/µg measured on a *previous* batch. The paper says this batch was not titrated. |
| D #9 ill | **Held if** | Held only by the job "the feed, not anything else, made #9 ill" — a job still in doubt (§4, rival a); a strain match would settle it. |
| E PrP^Sc + lesions | **Held** | Found in #9/#19 and the injected controls, in no other fed mouse. |
| F transmission | **Held** | A different kind of test from the feeding, and its prediction (only #9/#19 transmit) came true. |
| G non-transmitters | **Held if** | The job is "no hidden subclinical infection in feeders"; 2–3 mice per class. The paper itself raises the subclinical possibility, so this is the doubtful job. |
| H substrate control | **Held** | Rules out handling, cage and "any pellet does it". |
| I survives digestion | **Loose** | Nothing in the gut was measured. "Survived", "too few molecules reached the brain", or "wrong strain for the oral route" each do the same work for the 1-in-11 rate. |
| J rate comparable to natural prions | **Borrowed** | Compared across species, strains, routes and separate studies. |
| Conformation determines pathogenicity | **Borrowed** | Rests on cited biophysical work not tested here. |
| Enhancers (soil, colitis, M cells, mucosal cuts) | **Loose** | Offered as future work; no gauge, no poke. |
| "Particular strains and species" explain scrapie/CWD efficiency | **Loose** | A label: no change named that would show a strain *not* being the reason. |
| Group sizes, blinded scoring | **Unknown** | Paper never says how signs were scored or whether the scorer knew the group. Blind scoring with stated n would settle it. |

### 4. Whole-explanation checks

**Flip.** Suppose no fed mouse had fallen ill. Parts C and I would say "dose too low, digestion destroyed it" — the same parts cover both outcomes, so the rate explanation is doing less work than it looks. The existence claim itself survives the flip (one well-attested case suffices), but any claim that the *dose was adequate* does not.

**Direction.** The results run forward (feed → disease). The discussion runs backward, from the low rate and the transmitted disease to digestion and dose. Fine for "what can we tell", not for "what produced it". Say which is on offer.

**Answer hidden in the starting points?** Mostly no, and this is the paper's real strength: the pellet's PrP came from recombinant protein plus defined cofactors, so there is no route by which animal prions entered the feed. That is not the conclusion under another name.

**Pairs that pull.** "Rate comparable to natural prions" (so the dose was marginal) fights "recPrP^Sc has high titer" (so the dose was ample). The borrowed LD50 figure is leaned on in both directions; whichever gives way, say where the line is.

**Rivals.** (a) #9's illness was a spontaneous or cage-contaminant mouse prion, unrelated to the feed. (b) The dose reached #9 by a route other than swallowing — dried pellet on the mouth, grooming, inhaled dust. (c) The low rate is entirely dose/route, not a property of recPrP^Sc. Distinguishing changes: compare the fed conformer with the PrP^Sc from #9 (a); wrap the pellet so it must be swallowed (b); feed a measured dose series (c).

**Patches.** No quiet narrowing found: the paper states the 1-in-11 rate plainly, and the second round was added to test the subclinical alternative — a patch that does another job. Its weak point is that only a few mice per donor class were used.

**Where the parts came from.** The design — substrate control, two-round transmission, three donor classes — is **built**, and it committed itself in advance (only #9/#19 should transmit); it was not caught out. The dose arithmetic and the rate comparison are **fitted** to past studies and **borrowed**. "Digestion degrades PrP^Sc" is **asserted** from a citation. The jobs I added, not the owners': strain-matching #9 against the feed, and blinded scoring.

### 5. What would make it harder to vary

1. Match the PrP^Sc in #9 to the fed recPrP^Sc by conformation or strain. This is the single biggest gain — it kills rival (a).
2. Titrate *this* batch by injection and feed more mice at known doses, turning C from borrowed into measured, and testing the "more dose, more cases" half of the poke.

### 6. What this does not show

Hard to vary is not true. Two failures above are looseness, not error — "survives digestion" may be right and is simply unheld. Passing would not have proved the prion hypothesis, and this paper does not prove it.

### 7. One next step

Strain-type the PrP^Sc in #9 (and #19) and compare it with the conformer that was fed.
